subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats support automatic sender/role-specific subagents with isolated skills, config, and memory, or should OpenClaw keep group isolation at the current session/binding layer for now?
rationale: The remaining request changes group-chat orchestration, memory/security boundaries, and config/lifecycle policy; source inspection can show the gap but cannot choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design opt-in plugin mode
options.body: Define a Feishu-owned, default-off group subagent mode with limits, cleanup, permissions, and upgrade/docs requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep session-layer isolation
options.body: Document sender-scoped group sessions plus DM dynamic agents as the supported approach and reject automatic group subagents for now.

options.title: Route to plugin experiment
options.body: Ask for a ClawHub or external Feishu plugin experiment first, then bring back a core/plugin API gap only if current seams are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in plugin mode
recommendation.body: Define a Feishu-owned, default-off group subagent mode with limits, cleanup, permissions, and upgrade/docs requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The package identifies @m1heng as the Feishu community maintainer, making them the best routing candidate for the channel-specific product decision.
